title: Manifest
description:
The `.zpkg.toml` manifest at the root of every package repository.
TOML only — never YAML or JSON.

```toml
[package]
org = "acme"
name = "http-kit"
version = "1.2.0"
description = "Tiny HTTP helpers"
license = "MIT"

[package.repository]
vcs = "git"
url = "https://github.com/acme/http-kit"

[dependencies]
"acme/logkit" = "^0.3"

[publish]
exclude = ["benches/**"]
smoke_test = "sh scripts/smoke.sh"
```

dependencies.description: Dependencies keyed by `org/name`, valued by a semver requirement.

name.description: Package name, unique within the org. Lowercase slug.

org.description: Namespace the package is published under. Lowercase slug.

version.description:
Version of this package, interpreted according to `version_scheme`
(semver by default).

version_scheme.description:
How `version` (and published tags) should be interpreted. Semver by
default; `calver` for calendar versions, `opaque` for arbitrary tags.

exclude.description: Extra glob patterns to exclude on top of the built-in defaults.

include_readme.description: Keep README files in the published artifact (stripped by default).

smoke_test.description:
Command run by `zed test-local` inside a throwaway consumer project
that has this package installed the same way a real consumer would.

tag_format.description:
VCS tag template that must exist and point at the published commit.
`{version}` is substituted with `package.version`.

RepositorySection.description:
Where the package's source of truth lives. Any Git or Mercurial host
works: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or a self-hosted server.

test.description:
Test command run from the repository (not from published artifacts;
tests are stripped at publish time).

Vcs.description:
Version-control systems a package's source repository can live on.

zed-pkg is VCS-agnostic by design: what gets installed is always a
registry artifact, and the VCS is where provenance (tags) is anchored.
Authors must create a matching tag on their declared backing repo
(GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Codeberg, SourceHut, Forgejo, Gitea, Azure
DevOps, CodeCommit, Radicle, or self-hosted) before publishing.

`jj` and Sapling are git-compatible and push to git remotes, so their
provenance is verified through git tags.

VersionScheme.description:
How a package's `version` string (and its published tags) should be
interpreted. Defaults to [`VersionScheme::Semver`], which covers the vast
majority of modern ecosystems.

oneOf.description:
Semantic Versioning. `package.version` must be valid semver; ranges
(`^1.2`, `>=0.2 <0.5`) resolve to the max satisfying stable version.

Calendar Versioning (`2026.07.24`, `2026.07`). Normalized to a semver
total order (leading zeros dropped, padded to major.minor.patch) so the
same range algebra applies. See [`normalize_calver`].

Arbitrary tags (`release-candidate-1`, `legacy-api`). No range algebra:
a requirement must match a published version **exactly**.
